# Carl Meredith

## Overview

- **Age:** Nine years old when first introduced
- **Gender:** Male

## Appearance

Carl is a small boy with a quiet, solemn, pale face. He has fair hair and very round, sweet, big blue eyes. Even when indulging in antics or mischief, he maintains his serious expression.

## Personality

Carl is a quiet and somewhat solemn boy who possesses a deep, obsessive passion for bugs and small animals. He is generally good-natured, polite, and obedient when directly addressed, though he often forgets instructions when engrossed in his collections. Despite his angelic appearance, he possesses an appetite for bizarre antics, such as collecting dead creatures or crawling on his stomach. He remains unbothered by bugs or slimy creatures, handling them with affectionate fascination.

## Traits

- Fascinated by bugs and small creatures
- Quiet and solemn
- Absent-minded about household rules

## Abilities

- Collecting and caring for insects, reptiles, and small animals

## Goals

- To collect and keep various insects, frogs, toads, and pet animals

## History

Carl moves to Glen St. Mary when his father, John Meredith, becomes the minister of the Presbyterian church. He spends much of his time exploring the outdoors and collecting bugs, caterpillars, and spiders, which he frequently brings into the manse to the dismay of Aunt Martha and church visitors. Carl becomes a member of the Good Conduct Club formed by the Meredith and Blythe children to improve their behavior through self-imposed punishments. During one initiation dare, Carl eats a dead spider on a dare from his brother Jerry, which leads to a severe illness and pneumonia. The community rallies around the family, and Carl eventually recovers. When his father marries Rosemary West, Carl gains a loving stepmother who supports his interest in natural history, even building a box to house his pet toad.

## Background by volume

- Son of the Glen St. Mary Presbyterian minister, John Meredith
- Mother died when he was young, leaving him and his siblings under the care of Aunt Martha and a distracted father
